notes: This record is written once. Any modification after this point invalidates the confirmatory claim.
The hash is recomputed from in-memory PROTOCOL at the end of the notebook (Cell 13) and asserted equal.
Sub-artifact hashes are recorded for external audit.
If cohort size is below N_req, status is EXPLORATORY; this is a declared outcome, not a protocol modification.

protocol.arm_B_definition: SRDF threshold re-reading on matching S04/S06 splits. Recompute RF@pi_hat only. Integrity check: recomputed RF@0.5 must match recorded baseline_bacc within tolerance T=0.005. Interpretive, no p-value.
protocol.arm_L_definition: LogisticRegression(L2, C=1, max_iter=2000, class_weight optional) as alternative learner on the same splits. Four matched arms (A1_LR, A2_LR, A4_LR, A6_LR). Exploratory, no p-value.

arms.A2: RF@pi_hat (primary control; pi_hat = training minority prevalence)
arms.A7: RF@t_star (test-optimal oracle; diagnostic upper bound only)

declarations.sesoi_justification: 0.02 bAcc is the smallest difference that could plausibly change the ranking of two methods in a published comparison table where adjacent-method gaps are typically 3-10 pp.

protocol.h1_rule: One-sided sign-flip test of mean(Delta_thr) against +SESOI (0.02). SUPPORTED if p_holm < alpha; else NOT SUPPORTED.
protocol.h2_h4_rule: TOST against +/- SESOI with sign-flip permutation. EQUIVALENT if p_holm < alpha; else SUPERIOR if CI95_low > +SESOI; else INFERIOR if CI95_high < -SESOI; else INCONCLUSIVE.
protocol.h3_rule: Descriptive: win-flip rate with 95% bootstrap CI. Labels: reversed / attenuated / preserved / none. No p-value.
limitations: The study does not claim SRDF is better or worse than any baseline. SRDF appears only as one documented instance of the practice under test.
No claim extends beyond RF-based pipelines and OpenML binary tabular datasets within the declared size range.
Results are not extrapolated to missingness above 5%, to datasets with IR < 3, or to F1 / PR-AUC.
The hypotheses are not blind: S05/S06 data already suggest the direction of H1. This is disclosed, and the design is built so that the other outcomes remain meaningful.
OpenML metadata and datasets can change after the snapshot; content hashes of every fetched dataset are recorded for audit.

preprocessing.note: Ordinal encoding for all arms. One-hot is not used. SMOTENC receives integer-coded categorical features via declared categorical column indices.

research_questions.Q1: How much of the reported benefit of rebalancing over a plain classifier is an artifact of the default 0.5 threshold of the control?
research_questions.Q2: After replacing the control with the same learner at a parameter-free, prior-corrected threshold, does any rebalancing family retain a benefit, remain equivalent, or fall behind?
research_questions.Q3: In which regimes (IR, minority size, categorical share) does a residual benefit exist?

contribution_scenarios.A: Inflation is confirmed (H1 supported) and rebalancing is equivalent or inferior to the threshold-corrected control (H2 returns equivalence or inferiority for at least two of three methods).
contribution_scenarios.B: Inflation is confirmed but a residual benefit exists in defined regimes (H1 supported, H2 returns superiority for at least one method).
contribution_scenarios.C: H1 is not supported. The conventional control is adequate on this cohort. This is itself a methodological result.

success_criteria.definition: A clean execution plus a determinate (non-inconclusive) resolution of H1 and of H2/H4 for at least two of the three methods.
success_criteria.failure_definition: An integrity abort, or an inconclusive outcome on H1 and on all of H2.

protocol.title: Does Class-Imbalance Correction Beat a Threshold-Corrected Control? A Catalog-Wide Confirmatory Study of Benchmark-Practice Bias

status_note: Cohort size (131) meets the power requirement (N_req = 70). Confirmatory claims are permitted.
